findings.failure_mode: missing file or permission error causes process abort instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: Return a typed LoadError (Io variant), use map_err on fs::read_to_string, propagate Result

findings.problem: println! inside parsing logic leaks I/O into what should be pure data transformation
findings.failure_mode: side effects prevent deterministic testing, make output ordering dependent, and violate Functional Core / Imperative Shell
findings.fix: Remove println! from the parser; return log data if logging is needed; shell layer emits logs

findings.problem: parts[0] unchecked indexing into split result without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: malformed line with no commas causes panic at runtime
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') to destructurally get two fields with .ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) fallback

findings.problem: parts[1] unchecked indexing into split result without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: line with only one comma-separated field panics at runtime
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') for two-field destructuring instead of split/collect/get indexing

findings.problem: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 performs lossy cast from u32 to u16
findings.failure_mode: values in range 65536-4294967295 silently truncate to u16 range, producing incorrect domain values without any validation
findings.fix: Parse directly as u16 with parse::<u16>().map_err(ParseError::InvalidValue), or use u32::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(ParseError::Overflow)

findings.problem: load_packets fuses file I/O, logging, parsing, and collection in one function with no error type
findings.failure_mode: no separation of pure parsing from I/O shell; caller cannot handle specific error modes; function is not testable with synthetic input without filesystem access
findings.fix: Split into (1) parse_record(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> (pure core) and (2) load_packets(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> (shell that does I/O)

findings.problem: load_packets returns Vec<Record> with no error type; all failures silently panic
findings.failure_mode: IO errors, parse errors, out-of-range values, and malformed lines are indistinguishable and all manifest as panics
findings.fix: Define enum LoadError { Io(io::Error), InvalidRecord { line: usize, reason: ParseError } } and parse::ParseError { Empty, Invalid, Overflow, Allocation }

findings.problem: No capacity cap or try_reserve on the output Vec; unbounded file input can allocate unbounded memory
findings.failure_mode: large or adversarial input files cause unbounded heap allocation and potential OOM
findings.fix: Add max_records: usize parameter; call out.try_reserve(max_records).map_err(|_| LoadError::Allocation)? before the loop

findings.problem: split(',').map().collect() allocates a Vec for every line when only two fields are needed
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary per-line allocation; extra fields beyond two silently ignored; no structural guarantee of exactly-two fields
findings.fix: Use let (name, value_str) = line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)?; then parse value_str directly

findings.problem: Record uses pub name: String and pub value: u16 with no validation invariants
findings.failure_mode: any caller can construct Record with empty name string or any u16 value, including domain-invalid states
findings.fix: Use newtype name: NonEmptyString, hide struct fields, and provide Record::new(name: &str, value: u16) -> Result<Record, ParseError> smart constructor
